AVOID IF HUNGRY!! No Moroccan food
Apr 2019 • Friends
This may have been a Moroccan restaurant in the past but it certainly is not one now. It is a Shisha bar. 

The one page menu has some basic "Mediterranean fusion" foods which is just Vietnamese knock off crap which you can find anywhere. "Short rib fingers, t-bone steak, prawns". None of them are authentic Moroccan dishes as far as I'm aware. 

The setting wasn't ugly, but again, not for a restaurant. The seating is low sized, L-shaped sofas with long cushions which is not suitable for dining.

On their facebook page they have pictures of some really delicious looking MOROCCAN food, happy smiling customers and a Moroccan chef. Sadly this just for advertising purposes ie fake.

One more thing - looking at the other reviews on this trip advisor - the majority of them look fake. 

Go to Casablanca instead.

Arabian Fright
Oct 2018 • Couples
What a shocker. Booked a table for a Friday night as we thought it was going to be busy. Upon arrival we could see that the 'restaurant' was fairly quiet. It's divided between a well designed, cosy interior area and a rather uncomfortable L-shaped courtyard. Having booked we expected our choice of table. However, this wasn't the case. We were seated outside at a table so far in the corner we were basically in the kitchen. It took the allure right out of the rustic Arabic ambience. Having not settled for this table, and pressed the staff to move us inside, we were finally found a table that was more like what we expected. That's when the real fun started. The drinks order went without a snag. Unfortunately that was the only thing that did. To cut a long story short, we waited around 90 minutes to receive both starters - during this time we were moved into another corner to accommodate another group of guests. Hummus was the first thing we ordered but we had to ask again and again - perhaps 6 or 7 times in total - when this would be coming out. I assume they had to send someone half way to Casablanca to buy chickpeas. We had to reorder our mains several times and nearing the 2-hour mark we had become extremely hungry. It's worth mentioning that the Moroccan pizza was as dry as a camel's sock, and certainly not a satisfying starter. Eventually we grabbed the attention of the owner who assured us he'd spoken with his kitchen staff about the complete catering catastrophe thus far. There were many tables around us that had arrived during our wait, and had eaten their food by this point. Finally one main dish arrived. But no second main dish. The owner chose this as the moment to tell me they were missing several key ingredients to the chicken tagine. Maybe a competent chef was one of the ingredients he was referring to. We tried the lamb shish and it was what can only be described as Stone Cold Steve Austin. This was the straw that broke the camel's back. We promptly demanded a 30% reduction on our bill and for the mains to be removed altogether. After some deliberation, the owner reluctantly agreed. This place is perfect if you want to sit with a diet coke, smoking a hookah whilst taking infinite selfies. But a Moroccan restaurant, it ain't.

Perfect place to escape Asia!
Aug 2018 • Friends
I celebrated my birthday here and everyone was really helpful and happy to help you. The staff can speak English and offered excellent customer service. Every time we needed something they were readily available to help you. The food was incredible even for vegetarian. Peri peri was to die for! The melon ice cream was also superb. Belly dancing was also fun! I wish they could’ve dance more, they only danced twice and it was amazing. My friends really had a great time and they asked me how I managed to discover this place. It’s a hidden gem in Saigon! I will surely come back! Massive thanks for the wonderful staff who were very kind and helpful to me when I celebrated my birthday.
